h1: Kiatthada Resort — A Quiet Garden Retreat in Lat Phrao, Bangkok's Best-Value Muay Thai Stay
intro: Lat Phrao is where real Bangkokians live — less tourist-polished, more price-honest. Kiatthada Resort has sat on Sukhonthasawat Road in inner Lat Phrao for over 20 years, and its main selling point is simple: a genuine garden-resort atmosphere that hotel towers in this budget bracket simply cannot match. Add an internationally recognised Muay Thai camp (Khongsittha) and an indoor Golf Simulator on the same grounds, and you have something genuinely unusual for a property starting at around ฿600 per night.

body.html: A 20-year-old resort that still delivers — Kiatthada Resort opened in the early 2000s on Sukhonthasawat Road, about 2 km from the Ha Yaek Lat Phrao intersection, with Big C Lat Phrao a short drive away. The property spans 80 rooms across a low-rise compound with genuine garden space — a rarity among Bangkok budget options. The guest review that comes up most often is some variation of "couldn't believe I was in the middle of Bangkok, it was so quiet" — which, at this price point, is genuinely hard to find.

Rooms and what you actually get — There are four room categories: Superior King and Superior Twin rooms (both 30 sqm), straightforward and well-suited to solo travellers or couples on a budget; a Suite with Balcony at 60 sqm with a private balcony and separate seating area — consistently called out in reviews as "surprisingly large for the price"; and a Connecting Room (two King rooms adjoining) for families or small groups. All rooms have air conditioning, a flat-screen TV, mini-fridge, kettle, and free Wi-Fi. Garden-view rooms with balconies are the crowd favourite. One honest caveat: a handful of reviewers note that room photos on booking platforms don't always match the actual room assigned — worth clarifying with front desk when you book.

"Room was large, spotless and great value. AC was cold, Wi-Fi solid, bed comfortable. Peaceful atmosphere unlike any budget hotel I've stayed in Bangkok. Just know you'll Grab everywhere — no skytrain nearby."

The on-site extras that set it apart — The headline feature is Khongsittha Muay Thai, a camp with a genuine international reputation operating on the resort grounds. Guests can drop in for group sessions or book private training with champion-level coaches and fighters. Beyond Muay Thai, there's an indoor Golf Simulator, a billiard table, a gym (free to use), and a shared kitchen where you can heat or cook your own meals. The shared kitchen has earned particular praise from long-stay guests and digital nomads who want to keep food costs down without giving up comfort.

Location and getting around — know before you book — Kiatthada Resort sits at 11 Sukhonthasawat Road, set back from the main Lat Phrao strip. There is no walkable BTS or MRT station — the nearest (MRT Phahon Yothin / Ha Yaek Lat Phrao) is around a 10–15 minute Grab or motorbike-taxi ride. Multiple reviewers mention this as the biggest trade-off. For guests with their own transport or those who are comfortable using Grab, it is a non-issue. The immediate neighbourhood has a convenience store, local restaurants, and a market within walking range; Big C Lat Phrao is minutes away by car.

Scores, service, and what guests say overall — Trip.com aggregates 141 reviews at 8.0 out of 10, with Cleanliness scoring 8.2, Location 8.1, and Service 7.9. Booking.com (27 reviews) comes in at 7.1, which reflects a smaller, more mixed sample. Standout staff mentions — K. Nan, Emma, and Bambi at front desk — appear in multiple independent reviews praising responsiveness and friendliness. The most consistent complaints are: no full restaurant on-site (only a small cafe and shared kitchen), breakfast requires advance ordering, no swimming pool, and occasional room-photo-to-reality discrepancies. Nothing dealbreaking for the right guest, but important to know.

Bottom line — Kiatthada Resort is the right choice if you want a quiet, clean, garden-atmosphere base in Lat Phrao at under ฿1,000 per night, especially if Muay Thai training or an independent long-stay lifestyle is part of the plan. It is not the right choice if you need walking distance to a skytrain, a swimming pool, or a full-service restaurant. With rooms from approximately ฿600–900/night for Superior categories and up to ฿1,100–1,500 for the Suite with Balcony, the value-to-space ratio is among the best you'll find in inner Lat Phrao at this star level.

honestSummary: Kiatthada Resort is genuinely good value for the right traveller — spacious clean rooms, rare garden calm, and a world-class Muay Thai camp on the grounds, at prices that undercut most of central Bangkok. The honest trade-off is that the location demands reliance on Grab, there is no pool, and no full restaurant.
honestChecks: If you need walkable BTS or MRT access — the nearest station is 10–15 minutes by Grab; there is no pedestrian route → consider The Quarter Ladprao by UHG instead, which sits steps from MRT Phahon Yothin
If you want a swimming pool or in-house restaurant — Kiatthada Resort has neither → step up to Synsiri Ladprao 130 or a mid-range option with full facilities
If you're here for Muay Thai training or a budget long stay — this is exactly the right pick: quiet, clean, large rooms, Khongsittha camp on-site, shared kitchen, free parking → book with confidence

tips.title: Book Muay Thai sessions in advance
tips.body: Khongsittha Muay Thai accepts walk-ins but private coaching slots fill fast. Contact the resort before arrival to schedule sessions around your check-in and check-out dates.

tips.title: Plan your transport with Grab
tips.body: From the hotel, Grab to Ha Yaek Lat Phrao (MRT Phahon Yothin) takes about 10–15 minutes. From there you can reach Chatuchak, Ratchada, and central Bangkok easily by rail.

tips.title: Stock up at Big C Lat Phrao
tips.body: Big C Lat Phrao is a short drive away — ideal for picking up food, drinks, and supplies to use in the shared kitchen and keep your daily costs low during a longer stay.

tips.title: Request a garden-view room
tips.body: When booking, ask front desk for a room overlooking the garden — most positive reviews specifically mention the garden view as what makes the resort atmosphere feel genuine.

faq.q: Where is Kiatthada Resort located, and is it near BTS or MRT?
faq.a: Kiatthada Resort is at 11 Sukhonthasawat Road, Lat Phrao, Bangkok 10230. There is no walkable BTS or MRT station nearby — the closest is MRT Phahon Yothin (Ha Yaek Lat Phrao) at around 10–15 minutes by Grab or motorbike taxi. Best suited to guests with their own transport or who are comfortable using Grab regularly.

faq.q: What are room prices at Kiatthada Resort?
faq.a: Superior King and Twin rooms start from around ฿600–900 per night in standard periods. The Suite with Balcony (60 sqm) runs approximately ฿1,100–1,500/night. Prices vary by platform and season — comparing Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com before booking is recommended.

faq.q: Can beginners train at Khongsittha Muay Thai on-site?
faq.a: Yes. Khongsittha Muay Thai welcomes complete beginners as well as experienced fighters. Group classes and private coaching sessions with champion-level trainers are available. It is advisable to contact the resort or camp in advance to schedule sessions around your stay.

faq.q: Does Kiatthada Resort have a swimming pool or restaurant?
faq.a: No swimming pool and no full-service restaurant. There is a small cafe and a shared kitchen where guests can heat or prepare their own meals. Breakfast requires advance ordering and is not a buffet. The surrounding area has convenience stores and local restaurants within easy reach.

faq.q: Who is Kiatthada Resort best suited to?
faq.a: Best suited to Muay Thai enthusiasts and athletes, digital nomads seeking quiet affordable accommodation, long-stay travellers, and anyone comfortable relying on Grab for transport. Guests wanting a pool, full restaurant, or walkable rail access should consider a different property in the Lat Phrao corridor.
